subject: biology
title: Genetics Adventure 3: Mutation, gel electrophoresis and biotech
welcome_lead: Today you'll cut DNA with restriction enzymes and run a gel.
meta_desc: Biology — mutation types, gel electrophoresis, PCR, GM organisms, ethics.
final_note: You learned mutations include point and frameshift, gel electrophoresis separates DNA by size, PCR amplifies, and GMOs raise ethical questions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
DNA changes during replication or by mutagens (UV, X-rays, chemicals):

- Silent — base change, same amino acid (code degeneracy).
- Missense — base change, different amino acid (e.g. sickle-cell GAG→GTG = Glu→Val).
- Nonsense — base change creates STOP.
- Frameshift — insertion/deletion shifts all codons after the site.

DNA fragments are loaded into an agarose gel and an electric field applied. DNA is negatively charged (phosphate backbone) — fragments move to the anode.

Smaller fragments travel further. Compared to a ladder of known sizes, fragment lengths can be measured. Used in DNA profiling (Jeffreys, 1984).

PCR uses Taq polymerase, primers, dNTPs and thermal cycling (denature 95°C → anneal 55°C → extend 72°C). Each cycle doubles DNA — n cycles → 2ⁿ copies.

GM crops like Bt maize carry a bacterial toxin gene. Ethical concerns: ecological impact, gene flow, monopoly seed patents. International perspective: GMOs widely grown in USA + Brazil, restricted in EU.
